meta_title: Security and privacy: exact permissions, nothing more
meta_description: Baton's security architecture: explicitly scoped GitHub permissions, signed webhooks with HMAC-SHA256, session encryption, and strict data isolation.
h1: Exact permissions. No stored source code.
intro: Baton is built to request only the permissions it uses. Contents is read only so Baton can describe repository structure, and nothing it reads is retained. Baton never accesses production secrets or workflow definitions.
principle_webhook_body: Every incoming GitHub webhook delivery is authenticated against your configured webhook secret using HMAC-SHA256 with the x-hub-signature-256 header. Signatures are evaluated in constant time to prevent timing side-channel attacks before any JSON payload is parsed.
principle_retention_body: We store only operational metadata required to render the dashboard and measure stall durations: pull request titles, numbers, author logins, and timestamps. On uninstall, all pull request snapshots and repository configurations are deleted immediately and permanently.
principle_tenant_body: Every dashboard query is strictly scoped to the authenticated GitHub OAuth user and the installations they own or belong to. Sessions are backed by 32 cryptographically random bytes, hashed with SHA-256 before storage, and protected by httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies.
principle_disclosure_body: If you identify a security vulnerability in Baton, notify us immediately at security@baton.dev. We acknowledge reports within 24 hours and commit to transparent patching and public attribution.
cta_title: Need a custom security review or SOC2 report?
cta_body: Our Organization plan includes vendor assessment assistance, SAML SSO, and audit log exports.
row_1_purpose: Read review state, then update the single pinned status comment and send nudges.
row_1_stored: Titles, numbers, author logins, and timestamps
row_2_purpose: Manage the baton state label on the pull request.
row_3_purpose: Read check conclusions so Baton never nudges reviewers on a failing build.
row_4_purpose: Read repository names, owner logins, and the default branch.
row_5_purpose: Read the file tree, package manifest, and CODEOWNERS to describe how a repository is built.
row_5_stored: Nothing. Reads derive facts and are discarded.
row_6_purpose: Baton never requests Workflows or Secrets, so it cannot view secrets or CI definitions.
row_7_purpose: Baton cannot modify repository settings, invite members, or manage organization keys.
